source: Capacity Market T-4 auction for delivery 2029/30 (auction monitor report, Deloitte for DESNZ)
method: clearing price per kW of de-rated capacity x 1,000 kW per MW; the stack then multiplies by the storage de-rating factor for the duration
quote: The Clearing Price of the 2025 T-4 Auction was equal to £27.10, with the aggregate Bidding Capacity of Capacity Agreements of 40,108.608 MW. (Deloitte LLP, 12 March 2026)
derivation: GBP 27.10/kW/yr x 1,000 = GBP 27,100/MW/yr of de-rated capacity, the same for every duration. Cross-check: NESO 'Capacity Market Auction Capacity and Cost' (resource b1b58919-eaa4-40ea-80df-3d3e526f8223), 2029/2030 row: Forecast Cost GBP 1,086,943,277 / 40,108.608 MW = GBP 27.10/kW.
note: Most recent T-1 (delivery 2026/27, held 3-4 March 2026) cleared at £5.00/kW/yr (https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/media/69aedeaf6827004e30b8a56e/T-1-2025-for-delivery-2026-27-auction-monitor-report.pdf, Deloitte LLP, 6 March 2026: 'The Clearing Price of the 2025 T-1 Auction was equal to £5.00'). T-4 is used because a new build competes in T-4 for a multi-year agreement. Values are per unit of de-rated capacity; the de-rating factors are in data/assumptions/market.json.
cross_check: Modo Energy, "How does a battery energy storage system make money?", Neil Weaver, 19 May 2026 (updated 21 May 2026), https://modoenergy.com/research/en/how-does-battery-energy-storage-make-money: "Over the twelve months to April 2026, the Capacity Market contributed an average of £7,454/MW/year to GB BESS revenue, or roughly 10% of the stack." Not the same measure as ours: a fleet average of agreements already held (from earlier, higher-priced auctions), no duration stated; ours is what a new build would get in the 2029/30 T-4 (£27.10/kW x de-rating).
